summary: The bill creates a tax credit, capped at $100 million per taxpayer, for businesses that use U.S.-grown agricultural commodities to make food products sold without further processing, with the credit amount scaled to the share of domestic inputs and phased in over time based on a rising minimum domestic-purchase percentage.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates a new tax credit (up to $100 million per taxpayer) for using domestically produced agricultural commodities. This is a tax expenditure that reduces federal revenue and functions as a subsidy, thereby expanding effective government spending through the tax code rather than reducing it.

The core of the bill is an amendment to the Internal Revenue Code adding a new section 45BB that provides a tax credit equal to 25% of qualifying domestic agricultural input costs. This directly lowers the tax liability of eligible businesses, constituting a tax reduction for specific activities.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare coverage, insurance, providers, or medical services.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration, visas, border security, or pathways to citizenship.
The bill contains no provisions related to reproductive health, abortion access, or restrictions.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill contains no provisions addressing environmental regulations, emissions, conservation, or climate policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net benefits.
The bill contains no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The bill contains no provisions related to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.

The credit is available only for domestically produced agricultural commodities and phases in stricter domestic-content thresholds over time while excluding foreign inputs. This explicitly favors domestic production over imports and functions as a protectionist measure.
By enacting an uncapped (per taxpayer) tax credit without any offsetting revenue increases or spending cuts, the bill increases the deficit and does not prioritize debt reduction.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign aid or international assistance.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
The bill contains no provisions related to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill contains no provisions related to worker protections, wages, or union rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
